question: Project _______ is the world's first inter-continental large wild carnivore translocation project.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cheetah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Project Cheetah is the world's first inter-continental large wild carnivore translocation project, initiated in India.
 
• The project aims to reintroduce African cheetahs into India, where the species became extinct in 1952 due to habitat loss and overhunting.
 
• In September 2022, eight African cheetahs were brought to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh from Namibia under this ambitious conservation program.
 
• The project is part of India's broader wildlife restoration efforts and is executed in collaboration with international organizations and governments, including Namibia and South Africa.
 
• The goal is to establish a viable and secure population of cheetahs in India and restore their ecological role as top predators in the grassland and open forest ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lion**
 
 
• Lions are found in India primarily in the Gir Forest National Park, Gujarat, and are classified as Asiatic lions (Panthera leo persica).
 
• India has undertaken significant conservation efforts under the "Project Lion," focusing on habitat development, reducing human-lion conflict, and increasing their population.
 
• Unlike cheetahs, lions are not part of any inter-continental translocation project.
 
 
 
• **Crocodile**
 
 
• Crocodiles are large aquatic reptiles that inhabit rivers, wetlands, and coastal regions.
 
• In India, species like the mugger crocodile, saltwater crocodile, and gharial are found.
 
• India has conservation programs like the Gharial Conservation Project to protect the critically endangered gharial population.
 
• These efforts focus on breeding and reintroduction within their native ranges rather than inter-continental relocation.
 
 
 
• **Panther**
 
 
• The term "panther" often refers to melanistic leopards or jaguars, which are found in various parts of the world, including India.
 
• Leopards are widely distributed across India and are not subject to inter-continental translocation projects.
 
• Conservation efforts for leopards in India focus on mitigating human-wildlife conflict, habitat conservation, and anti-poaching measures.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Project Cheetah**
 
 
• This project is a significant step in wildlife conservation and biodiversity restoration.
 
• It also aims to raise awareness about the importance of protecting grassland ecosystems, which are often overlooked in conservation efforts.
 
• The initiative highlights India's commitment to global biodiversity goals under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).
